reasons.A: Keeps the author's dry, deadpan irony (the killing as 'a theological argument of a kind the farmers could understand') in brisk, confident sentences with a sardonic understatement at the close of a paragraph.
reasons.C: Has flashes of the same wry humour ('hard to defend anything without someone to tell you how') but turns earnest and apologetic at the end, softening the author's barbed stance with a measured, even-handed tone.
reasons.B: Plain, explanatory modern prose with little irony; its sentences are flat and it states the point sincerely rather than letting a sly punchline make it.
